title: Of the Civil Magistrate
subtitle: God has ordained civil rulers under him for his glory and the public good, armed with the sword to defend the good and punish evildoers.

paragraphs.text: God, the supreme Lord and King of all the world, has ordained civil magistrates to be under him, over the people, for his own glory and the public good. To this end he has armed them with the power of the sword, for the defense and encouragement of those who do good, and for the punishment of evildoers.

It is lawful for Christians to accept and execute the office of a magistrate when called to it. In their administration of that office, they ought especially to maintain justice and peace, according to the wholesome laws of each kingdom and commonwealth. To that end they may also, under the New Testament, lawfully wage war upon just and necessary occasions.

Civil magistrates having been set up by God for the ends just stated, we ought to render to them subjection in all lawful things commanded by them — in the Lord, not only for wrath but also for conscience' sake. We ought also to make supplications and prayers for kings and all who are in authority, that under them we may live a quiet and peaceable life in all godliness and honesty.
